usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Contacts live in your „Only me” area, each sealed separately: only you see them, on every device where you sign in. They do not go into areas, conversations or forms.
- Contacts (#/workspace/contacts): a list searchable by name, number, company, role, group and e-mail address; "groups" filter the list.
- In the „sms” edition the phone keeps a copy of them in a separate address book account „REcreatio” — thanks to it the name shows during a call. The copy is changed in recreatio, not in the phone's book; removing the „REcreatio” account from the phone removes only the copies.
- In the app's SMS the name from recreatio takes precedence over names from other phone accounts. The SMS archive in the browser labels numbers with names from your contacts, and „New message” suggests recipients from them.
- A group can have its own SMS number (SMS → „Numbers and groups”, #/workspace/sms/numery): whoever belongs to it gets SMS from that number, unless the conversation has its own choice. The number is tied to the group name — write it in "groups" the same as before.
- The import sends no SMS and does not change numbers assigned to groups.

json.title: Contacts as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
json.intro:
What the import does (Contacts → „More” → „Import and export (JSON)”):
- A contact with an "id" from the export is changed in place — only the fields in the document; the rest stays.
- A contact without "id" is looked up among existing ones: the same label (first and last name) and a shared number — then it is completed (new numbers, addresses, groups are added; what was there stays). Otherwise a new one is created.
- It deletes nothing. Before saving you see the list of changes and warnings.
- Everything is sealed in this browser — the service only sees that contacts exist. In the „sms” edition the phone gets a copy at the next save.
- For phones and Google keep using vCard („Load vCard”, „Save … as vCard”); JSON is for corrections by hand and by AI.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments, at most {max} contacts.
